To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Hand2 is expressed during enteric neurogenesis and in neurons expressing VIP and TH; 2) overexpression of Hand2 in ENS precursors increases neurogenesis and expression levels of VIP; 3) Hand2 is required for expression of VIP, and loss of Hand2 results in patterning defects in VIP neurons; and 4) Hand2 expression is not sufficient to induce TH expression in ENS precusors.
Hand2 is sufficient to promote neurogenesis and expression vasoactive intestinal peptide in the developing enterous system.
Hand2 is expressed during enteric neurogenesis in vivo and is sufficient and necessary to promote neurogenesis and expression and patterning of vasoactive intestine polypeptide‐positive neurons.

understanding how the enteric nervous systems (ENS) develops, how it is affected in disease and how it can be regenerated.

Hand2 is necessary for the development of enteric neurons, and that Hand2 is also sufficient for the development of a subset of enteric neurons.
